transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. It's really nice to meet you, too. Thank you so much for fitting me in. 

Um... well, I hope I'm not taking up your time for something silly, but... I guess what brings me in is that I have this... this feeling like I’ve got a motor humming right under my skin. It mostly happens whenever I’m supposed to just sit still. You know, like during the staff meetings at work—I'm a building cleaner—or during event briefings at my church. 

I try my best to be respectful and pay attention, I really do, but I always end up shifting in my chair a bunch, or I'll just stand up in the back, or find some little excuse to go move around. I'm not trying to be a bother to anyone or be disruptive, it's just... really hard for me to stay put. Is that... does that make sense to you? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Have there been times when you felt unusually high or euphoric?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. Like... like feeling really, really happy or on top of the world? 

No, I haven't ever really had anything like that. I'm sorry if that's not very helpful, but I'm usually just... well, pretty normal in my moods, I think. Aside from the fidgeting, anyway. I hope I'm answering that right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to know. But no, no unusual highs or anything like that.
When you were a child, did you already have a hard time sitting still?

Oh, um... well, yes, I suppose I did. I hope it doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid, because I really wasn't! I always wanted to be good for my teachers. 

But... I do remember getting into a little bit of trouble back in grade school for it. I had this habit of, well, popping out of my seat when I wasn't supposed to. And sometimes I'd accidentally talk over the teacher, or I'd start rushing ahead on my work before they even finished giving the directions. I never meant any disrespect by it, I promise, I think I was just... very eager, I guess? 

My mother used to say I acted like I was wound just a little too tight, even as a kid. Does... does that help? I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for.
Do you often feel worried or on edge even when you’re not expected to sit still?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I care about doing a good job, of course, and making sure the building is nice and clean for folks, but... I wouldn't say I'm a nervous person. 

I don't really walk around feeling scared or anxious or anything like that. It's really just that... well, that physical need to keep moving, rather than a worry in my head, if that makes sense? 

I hope it's okay that I don't have that symptom for you. I don't want to make your evaluation harder by saying no to these things, I just want to be as honest as I can. Am I doing alright with these questions so far?
